raw_response:
I will still do mostly what has worked for me, because 13.1 mu is not small enough to play around, and it is not big enough to waste money blindly. My main land will stay in wheat-maize, because with well irrigation that is still the safest way for me to keep grain and cash moving. I have seen improved wheat seed and hybrid maize do better than old seed when fertilizer and water keep up, so I will use those. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece, not too much, because it takes more watching and more spraying, and my family has off-farm work so labor is tight. On fertilizer, I would rather spend a bit more than come up short, especially on wheat topdressing and maize jointing stage. I will not start from zero; I will follow the usual local pattern, then adjust a little for my own field strength and water. For wheat I will push nitrogen a bit because irrigated land can carry it. For maize I will keep the stand full and feed it steadily. For cotton I will not overdo nitrogen early or it will grow too much stalk, so I will keep some potassium there to hold bolls better. Tillage-wise, I will keep things simple and save labor where I can: rotary before wheat, and no-tillage or very light work for summer maize after wheat harvest if moisture is right. That is how I will keep costs, labor, and yield in balance this year.
